observations: Photo 0 shows an engine and automatic transmission on a tiled floor with a brick wall background; ROLLS-ROYCE is cast on the side of the engine.
Photo 1 shows the same engine and gearbox from another angle with wiring, hoses, and the engine cover visible.
Photo 2 shows a top-down view of the engine with ROLLS-ROYCE clearly cast on the valve cover and a Rolls-Royce emblem on the cover.

claims.evidence: photo 0, photo 1, and photo 2 show ROLLS-ROYCE cast on the engine
no Cullinan badge, VIN, or model plate is visible in any photo
photos show the engine and gearbox but cannot confirm all ancillaries are present

risks.risk: Engine may be seized or internally damaged
risks.proof: video of the crankshaft turning by hand or with a starter, plus compression test

risks.risk: Missing turbos, ECU, wiring harness, or other ancillaries
risks.proof: itemized video showing every included component

risks.risk: Not actually from a Cullinan (could be Phantom, Ghost, or other Rolls-Royce)
risks.proof: VIN, registration, or build sheet linking the engine to a Cullinan
video of the transmission shifting or operating on a bench

risks.risk: Oil leaks, cracked block, or overheating damage
risks.proof: borescope inspection of cylinders and block

proof_requests: Video of the engine cranking or turning over by hand
Itemized video showing all included parts such as turbos, ECU, and wiring harness
Documentation or VIN proving the engine came from a Cullinan
Video of the transmission shifting or operating
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a Rolls-Royce engine and gearbox from the cast markings, so it can be priced at worst case as non-running and incomplete; the Cullinan origin cannot be proven from photos alone.
